name: One Relative Enlarged Row Makes the Two-Row Inverse Sound
statement: Let an ample two-row assembly $V=(B_0,D_0,D_1,B_1)$ have full-support forbidden reduction $H=(B_0,B_1)$, positive contraction $K=(D_1,D_0)$, and common intersection $C=B_0\cup B_1=D_0\cap D_1$. If either $D_0$ or $D_1$ peels to $C$, then $V$ is a pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness. It suffices that every connected component of the graph $2$-core of one $G(D_i\setminus C)$ have at most eight vertices. Hence a counterexample must have a $2$-core component of order at least nine in both enlarged rows.
proof: Delete a supplied relative row order inside its nonconstant row. Those words lie outside $C$, so they have no constant-row neighbours and retain exactly their row corner cubes. The remaining four rows form a one-row enlargement, up to exchanging the new coordinates, and hence form a forbidden family. The original and reduced outputs share the same negative reduction. Transporting the relative chain through each elementary operation, omitting repeated images, and appending a proper-minor peeling of the one-row output proves every proper minor positive. The forest/eight-facet relative theorem supplies the row peeling under the graph $2$-core condition.
